newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: VW SAYS FEBRUARY SALES UP 13 PERCENT.
newsitem.headline: VW SAYS FEBRUARY SALES UP 13 PERCENT.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG said on Tuesday that group sales rose 13 percent to about 660,000 vehicles in February and that sales so far for the year were doing well.

VW management board member Robert Buechelhofer told Reuters in an interview at the Geneva car show that sales in the critical west European market were up about seven to eight percent for the month over the 1996 year-ago period.

But he said sales were down about four to six percent in Germany during February, in part due to the suspension of production for about a week of VW's Polo model due to parts shortages caused by the Spanish trucker's strike.
Buechelhofer however noted that incoming orders in Germany for the first two months of 1997 were up 30 percent and that he expected the sales situation to stabilise in the country.
